title: Pushforward of constructible sheaves along finite morphisms
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X$ and $Y$ schemes of
finite type over $k$,
$f:X\to Y$ a
finite and finitely
presented morphism, and $\Lambda$ a finite ring annihilated by an
integer invertible on $k$, in the sense of
[sbc-def-coefficient-conventions]. If $F$ is a
constructible
$\Lambda$-module sheaf on $X_{\Et}$, then $f_*F$ is constructible
on $Y_{\Et}$, and $R^qf_*F=0$ for every $q>0$.

proof.text: Apply [fin4-thm-finite-morphisms-constructible] with $S=Y$. Its hypotheses hold because $Y$ is a finite-type $k$-scheme, $f$ is finite, and $F$ is constructible with coefficients as in [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions]. The chosen positive annihilator $N$ is invertible on $X$ and $Y$: its inverse in $k$ maps to an inverse under each structure map. The theorem gives that $R^qf_*F$ is constructible on $Y_{\Et}$ for every $q\geq0$.

Take $q=0$ in the preceding step. To identify $R^0f_*F$ with $f_*F$, use the module-sheaf direct image and its left exactness in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]: for an injective resolution $0\to F\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$, one has $\mathcal H^0(f_*I^\bullet)=\ker(f_*I^0\to f_*I^1)=f_*\ker(I^0\to I^1)=f_*F$. Thus $f_*F$ is constructible. For $q>0$, [fin4-thm-finite-morphisms-constructible] explicitly supplies $R^qf_*F=0$ for the $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$.
